title: Safety Nets
objective: After this level you can explain unemployment insurance, pensions and other safety nets.
summary: Germany created old-age social insurance in 1889. Unemployment insurance replaces part of lost wages. US Social Security is pay-as-you-go, strained as workers per beneficiary fall.

cards.headline: The world's first state pension started at age 70.
cards.body: In 1889, Germany, under Chancellor Otto von Bismarck, became the first nation to adopt old-age social insurance. It gave workers basic security from age 70, and workers, employers and the government all paid in. It was a net stretched under ordinary life.

cards.headline: Insurance for losing your job
cards.body: A safety net catches you when income suddenly stops. Unemployment insurance gives temporary, partial wage replacement to workers who lose their jobs through no fault of their own. Temporary, because it runs out; partial, because it covers only part of your old pay. In between, it helps people keep paying the rent and the bills while they look for work.

cards.headline: Today's workers, today's retirees
cards.body: US Social Security is one of Level 51's biggest federal items, and it works pay-as-you-go. The taxes today's workers pay fund today's beneficiaries; nobody's contributions sit in a personal pot. That makes one ratio matter a lot. In 1965, about four workers paid in for each beneficiary. By 2023, there were 2.7.

cards.headline: How should a net be designed? The trade-offs

items.label: Unemployment benefits
points: People receiving them still search hard for work
But longer benefits can lengthen unemployment somewhat

items.label: Pay-as-you-go pensions
points: Pay retirees straight from current workers' taxes
Come under strain as retirees grow relative to workers

cards.headline: Safety nets: explained
learned: Unemployment insurance: temporary, partial wage replacement
Pay-as-you-go: today's workers fund today's retirees
Fewer workers per retiree strains the system

questions.prompt: Who is unemployment insurance designed for?

options.label: Anyone who quits to start a business
options.rationale: It covers job loss through no fault of your own.

options.label: Workers who lose their jobs through no fault of their own
Only workers who never earned wages
options.rationale: It replaces part of lost wages, so it needs past wages.

questions.explanation: Unemployment insurance gives temporary, partial wage replacement to workers who lose jobs through no fault of their own.

questions.prompt: Why does the drop from about four workers per beneficiary to 2.7 matter for US Social Security?

options.label: Each retiree now has a bigger personal account
options.rationale: There are no personal pots: it is pay-as-you-go.

options.label: Fewer workers' taxes are funding each beneficiary
The ratio only affects private pensions
options.rationale: It matters precisely because Social Security is pay-as-you-go.

questions.explanation: In a pay-as-you-go system, today's workers fund today's beneficiaries, so fewer workers per beneficiary means more strain.

questions.prompt: From Level 51: which of the biggest US federal spending items is a safety net for retirees?

options.label: National defense
options.rationale: Defense protects the country, not retirees' incomes.

options.label: Highways
options.rationale: Mostly state and local spending, and not a safety net.

questions.explanation: Social Security is one of the biggest federal items, paid for by today's workers' taxes.
